stage: 6a. Run day to day: money (settlement, clearing, reconciliation, billing, interchange qualification, reporting)

summary.text: On every network studied, money runs on daily files and reports that the partner must reconcile itself. Visa issues VSS reports, Mastercard six GCMS cycles and Amex one Daily Activity Report.
Settlement and billing are separate streams. Mastercard bills weekly through MCBS, Visa invoices through its Online Invoice Portal, and both collect fees by ACH in the US.
The UK regulator found issuers generally cope with Mastercard and Visa fee information. Acquirers do not, so the pain concentrates on the acquiring side.
The weakest link is tying an invoice line to the transactions that triggered it. Portal bulletin codes do not match invoice codes, and some Visa bulletins omitted the billing event.
Visa and Mastercard each told the UK regulator they could not supply that fee logic within a year. Mastercard cited many billing events and poorly documented legacy systems.
Regulators are now setting a floor. UK rules require a unique billing identifier and fee logic from July 2027, and the RBA expects machine-readable invoices at no extra cost.

Interchange downgrades are found after the fact, in processor reports. Mastercard's parameter file lists rate designators but omits the rates, so acquirers cannot compute expected interchange from it.
American Express is the clearest public counterexample. Its GNS manual publishes settlement timing, fee amounts and two-way late compensation, and its merchant files state the net payment arithmetic.
Processors and programme managers fill the gap. Stripe and Lithic turn raw network files into settlement records with states, and vendors sell invoice analysis to acquirers and issuers.

The Discover family is split. PULSE sells a one-page invoice and single-point gateway settlement, while Discover keeps US acquirer rates confidential and misclassified cards for sixteen years without telling merchants.
The public record is thin on current settlement manuals, invoice layouts and analytics screens for all four networks. Most detail comes from processor republications and regulator files.

by_partner.partner_type: Issuers (large banks, community banks, credit unions)

how_it_works.text: Visa settles once a day per settlement service. Marqeta gives the default cut-off as 10:00 GMT in summer and 11:00 GMT in winter.
Clearing that arrives after cut-off is reported under a different settlement service heading, which a reconciler must know to match totals.
Money moves through a hierarchy of Settlement Reporting Entities. Clients must choose which level's network totals match their own institution setup.
Visa says most US dollar settlements complete the same day. It indemnifies members against another member's failure to settle and may require collateral.
Associate members hold their own licence but rely on a Principal for settlement, reporting and fee payment.

Fees are invoiced separately and collected by ACH under a signed authorisation. In the US Region, member fee collections move as transaction codes 10 and 20, within 45 calendar days for domestic transactions.
At a small credit union one manager can own daily card processing, settlement and general ledger reconciliation together.
Processors re-present the money in their own report codes. FIS report SD-056 nets interchange income against network fees by BIN-level product each day.
A member sets up each funds transfer point on paper Settlement Funds Transfer forms. Visa processes complete forms in about 30 days.
The settlement account must be open, funded and able to take Visa drawdowns before settlement starts. Visa moves no money for positions under USD 1.
A new settlement bank, account, currency or post-merger name needs a fresh set of forms. ABA or SWIFT changes go by signed letter on letterhead.
Non-dollar settlement pays two currency business days after processing. Visa's settlement bank sends the SWIFT debit request two days before value date.
A national settlement service may set a domestic cut-off between 01:00 and 10:00 GMT. Every member in that country must agree the time.
Members in those countries then receive two report sets a day. National reports arrive about an hour after the national cut-off.
A trial balance service gives settlement agents interim reports from an earlier cut-off, before the final international run.
VSS reports run seven days a week. Monthly fees and charges are calculated daily and held until the last calendar day of the month.
Visa asks three months' notice for a first VSS set-up and two months for a new funds transfer. Choices are recorded on paper worksheets.
Single Message System members can take an 0620 funds transfer totals message when settlement completes. First-time recipients certify over two days.

tools_and_screens.name: VSS-110 Settlement Summary
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Daily totals for interchange value, reimbursement fees and Visa charges, split by issuer, acquirer and other business modes, with a monthly VSS-110-M.

tools_and_screens.name: VSS report family (VSS-110, 115, 120, 130, 140)
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Settlement summary, entity recaps, interchange value, reimbursement fees and Visa charges, delivered as machine-readable TC46 and print-ready TC47 files.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Online Invoice Portal (VOIP)
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Invoices under Global Member Billing Solutions, with Invoice & Collection Summary, Collection Details, and Current Billing Summary and Detail sections.

tools_and_screens.name: VisaVue Online
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Benchmarks plus authorisation, fraud, fee and exception data, holding 25 months of portfolio data and 13 months of transaction data.

tools_and_screens.name: VSS report subscription
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Each SRE picks its own reports. Only VSS-110 is mandatory, for funds transfer points, and optional reports appear only when subscribed.

tools_and_screens.name: VSS-110 print layout
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Header names the reporting SRE, its roll-up SRE and the funds transfer entity. A funds transfer amount shows only for a funds transfer SRE.

tools_and_screens.name: VSS-100-W and VSS-100-R hierarchy lists
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: The settlement hierarchy under each SRE, with YES in a Funds Transfer column. Delivered on Thursdays and Sundays.

tools_and_screens.name: VSS-300, VSS-135, VSS-610, VSS-640 and VSS-950
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Financial recap per subordinate SRE, month-to-date reimbursement fees, pending fees and charges before month end, and a no-data notice for quiet subscribed reports.

tools_and_screens.name: Customised hierarchy checklist
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: An implementation checklist requiring, among other rules, a unique 15-character name for every SRE in a custom hierarchy.

tools_and_screens.name: SMS600 to SMS617 transaction and exception detail reports
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Daily lists of single message transactions, chargebacks, representments, adjustments and reversals. Each can be sorted by card, retrieval reference, time or counterparty ID.

tools_and_screens.name: SMS642 and SMS643 CRS Returned Exception Detail
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Exception items returned unsettled after failing Chargeback Reduction Service checks, with up to five return reason codes, ready to correct and resubmit.

tools_and_screens.name: SMS660 No Activity Report
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Each subscribed SMS report that had nothing to show in the cycle, so a missing report reads as no activity.

tools_and_screens.name: SMS detail report fee line
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Fee jurisdiction, routing, fee level name and fee programme indicator for each transaction, all supplied by Visa on optional line 5.

friction.text: Reading a Visa invoice needs knowledge of settlement and collection entities, which Visa teaches as a course.
Settlement reporting and reconciliation are sold as paid training webcasts.
Report selection is not self-serve for programmes behind a processor. Marqeta tells customers to ask their Visa representative which VSS reports they can receive.
Visa's rules make every US issuer pay Advanced Authorization fees whether or not it uses the data.
Settlement set-up and bank changes run on paper forms, letters and worksheets with lead times of weeks to months.
The interchange fee line on SMS detail reports is off by default. Changing report lines means contacting a Visa Member Services representative.

how_it_works.text: Clearing reaches issuers in six GCMS cycles a day, cut off in St. Louis time. Every customer must take data from all six.
Mastercard settles most customers Monday to Friday after the sixth cycle. Monday advisements carry Saturday, Sunday and Monday totals.
In the US the settlement agent pulls funds by Fedwire drawdown, which a BaaS guide times at 8:00 Central.
A new issuer signs a Net Settlement Agreement and must fund settlement and billing from the day its ICA is assigned, or face assessments.
MCBS bills weekly to each ICA and covers Mastercard, Cirrus and Maestro fees. US banks authorise ACH drafts for it.
Issuers tie out in layers, from dispute rows to the per-cycle position to PDS 0396, the net amount in the day's wire.
Processors re-present the bill. FIS report BIMCBSM001 lists Mastercard fees by service and event code with quantity, rate and amount to reconcile the monthly bill.
A principal joins settlement by filing the online Net Settlement Information Form in Mastercard Connect, under Support, Forms, Clearing & Settlement.
Mastercard wants the form 30 days before launch and needs ten business days to review, test and implement the parameters.
US dollar settlement cuts off at 08:00 St. Louis time, and funds owed are due by 14:00 the same day.
Funds transfers usually reach the settlement agent two to three hours after cut-off.
Positions under USD 1,000 can be held for up to ten business days. Some services opt in on Form 829, and others opt out on Form 814.
Principals must pay the exact advised amount, one payment per ICA and value date.
A disputed advisement must be raised in writing within one business day. The advised amount must still be paid on time.
Missed settlement draws a daily assessment from the first day, from USD 250 up to USD 10,000 by amount.

tools_and_screens.name: Pricing and Billing Resource Center (Mastercard Connect)
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Pricing Guide, Transaction Detail and a Billing Analytic Tool. Requested from the Connect Store and approved by the customer's Security Admin.

tools_and_screens.name: Operational Reports (Mastercard Connect)
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Invoices and further billing and pricing detail, recommended to sponsor banks by a BaaS provider.

tools_and_screens.name: GCMS cycle reports IP727010-AA, IP727020-AA, IP728010-AA
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Per-cycle acknowledgement, notification and summary reports, delivered as bulk type T140.

tools_and_screens.name: Mastercom eStats and T5G2 reconciliation
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Case fees totalled by billing event, and dispute clearing events for reconciliation.

tools_and_screens.name: Transfer Agent Advisement Detail (BSADV308-AA)
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Daily net position for the transfer agent bank, one section per member ID. Sent by Connect, email, fax or SWIFT MT998.

tools_and_screens.name: Member Advisement Detail (BSADV303-AA)
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: A reconciliation copy for members in a consolidated arrangement. It is not a payment instruction.

tools_and_screens.name: Transfer Agent Advisement Exception Report (BSADV309-AA)
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Payments held under the minimum threshold, with dates, amounts and cumulative value.

tools_and_screens.name: NSIF online form and NSIF Super User role
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Current settlement parameters on view. The role is ordered in the Connect Store and approved by the customer's Security Administrator.

tools_and_screens.name: Open Settlement Invoices email
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: An opt-in courtesy email about open or outstanding settlement positions and unapplied funds.

tools_and_screens.name: SWCHD412 Daily Interchange Report and SWCHM412 monthly
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Interchange by product and fee line, with counts split into financial, percentage-based, non-financial and non-billable. A Net Interchange Summary page closes it.

friction.text: Reports are themselves billed, each carrying a billing event. Recreating expired clearing data costs a per-file fee under event 2GC0001.
Mastercard Academy sells a two-day clearing, settlement and billing reconciliation workshop.
A dispute software vendor says issuers rebuild Mastercard fund reconciliation from documentation fragments and spreadsheets.
Changing clearing cutoffs goes through the Form 600 worksheet, and on release days early cycle files arrive one to three hours late.
Sponsor banks learn MCBS service codes, such as AB for issuer authorisation, from BaaS guides.
Missing a courtesy notice does not excuse non-compliance fees.
Held credit funds are released only on a written request carrying an original signature from the principal.
Settlement services are themselves billed monthly. In 2006 Mastercard even billed principal members for the debit settlement manual.
Mastercard Academy sold a two-day MCBS billing seminar for USD 900, invoiced through MCBS under its own billing event.

how_it_works.text: GNS runs one net settlement a day with each issuer and acquirer partner, reported on a mandatory Daily Activity Report.
Under Automated Funds Exchange a partner pays its net position the day the report arrives.
Monthly network fees sit in the report's Fee Detail Section by billing unit code and settle on the 26th.
A partner must pay the full reported amount even while disputing it. Late settlement in either direction earns compensation at a published cost-of-funds formula.
The manual publishes fee amounts, including $500 per late settlement, $175 a month per active BIN and $250 a month for portfolio reporting.

tools_and_screens.name: Daily Activity Report and Daily Activity File
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: The report is the consolidated reconciliation record. The optional file feeds a partner's own reconciliation and reporting systems.

tools_and_screens.name: Knowledge Base: Reporting Center, File Tracker, Program Progress Reports
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Partner applications for reports, file status, monthly programme returns, disputes and fraud.

friction.text: GNS partners must file monthly Program Progress Reports within 15 days of month end, with an annual attestation.
Settlement delays are notified by phone or fax and confirmed by certified mail.
GNS may withhold a partner's daily net settlement where it judges the financial or brand risk material.

how_it_works.text: Discover Debit is sold to community banks and credit unions on an all-in programme fee, a one-page invoice and no quarterly reporting.
A PULSE case study describes the all-in fee as the network fee on portfolio volume, with a two basis point discount for ABA members.
FIS client banks see PULSE fees in a monthly PIN fee report that points them to the PULSE Issuer Fee Schedule for definitions.
Diners Club cross-border transactions route and settle through a central service centre, and licensees hold primary liability to pay their own merchants.

tools_and_screens.name: PULSE Debit Dashboard
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Account overview led by Overall Gross Interchange, product pages for PULSE PAY, PULSE ATM and Gateway, and peer comparison.

tools_and_screens.name: PULSE client logins
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Debit Dashboard, ATM List Manager, Marketing Hub and PULSE Exchange.

friction.text: PULSE claims its all-in fee lets an issuer reconcile the monthly bill in about ten minutes. This is a vendor claim with no independent test.

how_it_works.text: STAR tells issuers it settles interchange daily and adds quarterly business reports by merchant category with gross interchange and fees.
SHAZAM markets real-time settlement on its single-message pathway and the lowest issuer switch fee, without publishing amounts.

tools_and_screens.name: FIS iQ Reports tab
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Coded daily and monthly settlement reports for banks and credit unions, kept for 90 days and searched in 60-day windows.

friction.text: ICBA told the Fed that most community banks struggled to get network and processing fee data from their technology providers. This is advocacy.
ICBA says technology providers' billing statements are long and hard to interpret, and many banks retain billing consultants.
Commenters told the OCC that core providers' bills are confusing and repeatedly wrong.
Vendors say issuers and acquirers mostly track network fees from raw invoices, processor summaries and spreadsheets.
An FIS posting for a scheme fee analyst describes recalculating fees from five schemes, Diners Club and Discover among them, and reconciling them to invoices.

best_pattern.text: Amex GNS puts settlement timing, exception handling, two-way late compensation and exact fee amounts in one public manual, so an issuer can predict its monthly bill.

discover_today.text: PULSE issuers get a one-page all-in invoice and a Debit Dashboard led by gross interchange. Settlement mechanics and fee schedules sit on the client site and appear publicly only through processor reports.

how_it_works.text: Visa assigns a Fee Program Indicator that places each transaction in an interchange programme. Transactions failing fee edits fall to Standard or named downgrade programmes.
Processors pre-qualify transactions before clearing. A Visa downgrade happens when Visa disagrees and reclassifies the transaction to a worse rate.
For settlement out-of-balance cases TSYS asks clients for VSS-110, 115, 120, 130 and 140 and tells them to register on each network portal, including Visa Online.
Interchange disputes between members run through IRF Compliance. One case can hold up to a million transactions, and Visa's decisions are final with narrow appeal.
Visa told the UK regulator that acquirers can reconcile using monthly invoices, an Acquirer Billing Guide launched in 2025 and Visa Client Services.
Processors can have each member's BIN stamped into VSS report records, so they can split the reports and pass them to client banks.
Reports reach BASE II members through the Edit Package, which prints them. Direct Access Service users receive file types such as SETLR.
SMS611 shows an acquirer each chargeback received, and Visa says it is used to decide whether to accept or represent.
Instead of reports, SMS members can take 130-byte raw data records. A settlement record per affiliate BIN carries the interchange total.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Access
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Visa describes a searchable database of client material with an analytics platform, a Support Hub, tutorials, webinars and FAQs.

tools_and_screens.name: VisaVue Online (acquirer)
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Interchange expense across merchant portfolios, alongside chargebacks, representments, fraud and fees.

tools_and_screens.name: Interchange Downgrade Detail (TSAD50F-1) and Returned Item Detail (EP-204A)
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: TSYS reports that show acquirers Visa downgrades and returned items with BASE II reason codes.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Integrity Detail Report
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Monthly detail explaining integrity fees, which Fiserv's pass-through schedule prices per item.

tools_and_screens.name: VCMS settlement test environment
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Test VSS reports delivered with TEST in the header. Requests need three weeks' notice, and BASE II acquirers may send 3,000 test transactions a day.

tools_and_screens.name: SMS609 Transactions Incurring a Fine
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Late adjustments, late deposit adjustments and chargebacks left unrepresented that drew a fine in the processing day.

tools_and_screens.name: SMS608 Fee Collection and Funds Disbursement Detail
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Fee collections and funds disbursements applied to settlement. Its totals feed the Other Transactions section of VSS-120, and its items appear on no other SMS report.

friction.text: One UK acquirer found 13 Visa bulletins in 2024 that did not show the billing event, so new fees surfaced first on the invoice.
Acquirers reported broken portal search and deleted historical billing information.
Downgrade and reject reports missing from a daily package cannot be recreated later. TSYS gives qualification problems a seven business day target.
Visa said transaction-level fee identifiers would need a complete overhaul of its global systems.
Visa's fixed acquirer network fee is assessed per merchant tax ID from locations, MCC and volume, so acquirers must allocate it themselves.
Member names on Edit Package reports come from a local setting and may not match the VSS report, which complicates matching.
A processor left out of the settlement hierarchy cannot receive the VSS-900 reconciliation reports.
SMS reports subtotal at every change of SRE, processor or affiliate BIN. An affiliate spread across several may need subtotals added by hand.
Raw data version 2.3 is a partial subset for reconciliation and cannot be taken alongside a version 2.2 subscription.

how_it_works.text: Acquirers send IPM files to GCMS, which edits, prices and routes them. A message failing an edit is rejected with no warning or adjustment path.
Interchange programmes carry timeliness, authorisation code, MCC and processing code rules. If the submitted rate designator fails, GCMS discards it and tries the next.
The US consumer credit Standard rate, where failing transactions land, is 3.15% plus USD 0.10.
Mastercard told the UK regulator that Connect gives acquirers near real-time consolidated billing and free tools on behavioural fees, plus a simplified invoice.
File exchange is set up through a parameters spreadsheet passed back and forth with Mastercard. The live list of bulk types arrives daily in the T007 file.
Debit switch reports reach processors as Global File Transfer bulk files or on screen in MasterCard eService. Online copies stay viewable for 13 months.
Each processor must reconcile its own batch totals to the switch every day. Mastercard urges an automated compare of the switch batch file with internal records.
Processors settling by ACH give their bank, routing number and settlement account on a Processor Information Questionnaire during sign-up.
A 2006 release added a BIN field to the daily control and interchange reports, so processors could sort settlement data by BIN.

tools_and_screens.name: IPM early reconciliation file (T113)
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Settlement position and errors for each file as soon as it is processed, before the next cycle cutoff.

tools_and_screens.name: Clearing Optimizer
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Software run on the customer's own hardware that applies GCMS edits before files are sent.

tools_and_screens.name: Mastercard Connect billing tools
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Consolidated billing in near real time and free behavioural fee reports, as Mastercard described them to the UK regulator.

tools_and_screens.name: Mastercard File Express Client and Scheduler
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Upload and download of production and test files, 30 days of archive retrieval, and a daily transfer log by result and endpoint.

tools_and_screens.name: Mastercard Data Exchange
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Browser file exchange with an Endpoint Summary Page of bulk file types. Users pick the endpoint by hand for each file.

tools_and_screens.name: SWCHD363 Daily Control Report and SWCHM363 monthly
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Net settlement position in the settlement currency, by transaction type within product. A Net Settlement Summary page nets transactions, exception items and interchange fees.

tools_and_screens.name: SWCHD586-A Debit Mastercard Inbound/Outbound Fee Report
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Retrieval, record clearing, handling and compliance fees sent and received, grouped by message type and function code, with a net fees page per processor.

friction.text: The parameter file acquirers receive lists rate designators but omits the rates, which Mastercard treats as proprietary.
Mastercard stopped phoning acquirers about risk rejects, and a sender with no confirmation file must phone to learn whether its file was processed.
One acquirer said fee code answers from Mastercard and Visa take four to five weeks.
One acquirer had eight Mastercard fee trigger misalignments in two years. Another reported Mastercard seeking to claw back several years of fees after its own error.
Mastercard's reporting schedule pushes one behavioural fee two months behind the transactions at Adyen.
File Express takes two to three weeks to implement. Mastercard warns that leaving file naming until network work ends causes delay.
A second SFTP session on the same user ID makes the first fail, and Mastercard gives no support for third-party SFTP software.
Mastercard warns that SWCHD412 interchange lines cannot be checked line by line where fees are percentage-based or acquirer generated.
Debit switch settlement reports leave out any transaction type with no activity that day. Mastercard also expects switch and processor totals to differ at times.

how_it_works.text: Under OptBlue, Amex settles with the Merchant Services Provider, which funds the merchant on its own plan and answers settlement questions.
OptBlue Participants pay Amex a wholesale discount rate plus programme fees and set the merchant's price themselves.
GNS acquirers are paid face value less a bilateral Network Rate. Clearing files are acknowledged and rejects return with up to ten reason codes.
OptBlue settlement is wired to the Participant the business day after submission. Friday to Sunday submissions arrive as three payments on Monday.
Submission files sent after 11:59:59 pm Mountain time count as the next business day.
Amex deducts the wholesale fee, chargebacks and credits from face value. Shortfalls are taken by ACH debit, then invoiced.
Amex keeps wholesale and additional fees on chargebacks and credits.
Both sides reconcile daily from the GRRCN file, where most fees land. Where records conflict, Amex records prevail.
A Participant that pays the wrong merchant must correct it within ten days. Merchant funding must match the speed of other networks.

tools_and_screens.name: GRRCN Seller ID
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: A 20-byte field that lets an OptBlue Participant or payment aggregator reconcile fees and pricing per sub-merchant.

tools_and_screens.name: OptBlue Additional Fees table
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Assessment, Acquirer Transaction, Inbound, CAPN Non-Compliance, Data Quality, data security and Excessive Chargeback fees, each described with its trigger.

friction.text: A bank acquirer republished OptBlue pricing tiers to merchants with its own network fee added on top.
The OptBlue Operating Regulations are marked confidential, yet an October 2024 copy is openly posted by a third party.
That posted copy describes each additional fee yet gives every amount only as a referral to the Participant.

how_it_works.text: Discover collects interchange and assessments from acquirers inside daily settlement.
Discover relies on acquirers to give merchants one statement with Visa and Mastercard, and may withhold settlement or take collateral from riskier merchants.
To claim misclassification refunds, acquirers submit tab or pipe delimited data files checked with a Data Validation Tool.

tools_and_screens.name: DGN service centre acquirer interchange page
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: The US table opens only with a verification code the acquirer issues and is marked confidential. Canada's schedule and network fees are public.

friction.text: From 2007 to at least 2023 acquirers and merchants paid commercial interchange on consumer cards without being told. About five million cards were affected.
The network had no classification controls, and misclassification is defined by Discover's own records, which acquirers could not see.
Refunds were hard to compute because agreements, network terms and historical data varied. Allocation notices are expected only in late 2026.
Adyen's public price list charges a blended rate for Discover and Diners, against interchange plus a margin for Visa and Mastercard.

how_it_works.text: The UK ITC Direction requires Mastercard and Visa to let acquirers see how each fee is triggered, reconcile invoices and allocate fees to UK transactions. Substantive duties apply from end of July 2027.
The August 2026 extension defers fee logic to July 2029 for fees earning £850,000 or less a year, but schemes must supply it free on request meanwhile.
Acquirers told the UK regulator they would pass most scheme fee increases to merchants at some point, whatever the contract type.

tools_and_screens.name: Torus and CardTraq network fee analytics
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Third-party invoice analysis, merchant-level allocation and flags for new or misapplied Visa and Mastercard fees.

friction.text: Acquirers with over 90% of the UK market reported difficulty understanding behavioural fees, and those with over 65% struggled to get timely answers.
Acquirers said they buy optional reporting to understand fees, and some said issues took months to resolve.
Teya said scheme billing lines can hold several hundred events, each taking hours to trace.
One firm keeps an invoice review team that found several million pounds of incorrect scheme charges in a year.
Australian providers said schemes charge for the reports needed to reconcile fees, and some absorb small billing errors because chasing them costs more.
Most RBA submissions said confidentiality terms stop participants comparing prices or understanding their own bills.
Acquirers staff this work. Shift4 and Stripe advertise analyst roles to reconcile scheme invoices and model new network fees.

best_pattern.text: The UK ITC standards set the bar. Each fee gets a unique billing identifier and free fee logic kept 12 months, with six months' notice and an impact model on request.

discover_today.text: Discover's US acquirer rates sit behind an acquirer-issued code while Canada's are public. The Fed now requires controls that classify and assess interchange for each acquirer and merchant.

how_it_works.text: Visa behavioural fees reach merchants as pass-throughs under processor descriptors, such as Misuse of Authorization, Zero Floor Limit and the Transaction Integrity Fee.
Visa replaced Level 2 and 3 with CEDP in October 2025. Only businesses Visa verifies for data quality get Product 3 rates at capture.

tools_and_screens.name: TSYS e-Connections exception reports
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Mis-Qual, Dis-Qual and Non-Qual qualification exception reports in the Portfolio Reporting module.

friction.text: Stripe's CEDP reports carry data from two months earlier.
Finix warns that poor CEDP data can downgrade past transactions, and a fee analytics firm saw merchants lose qualification where their acquirer had not finished certification.

how_it_works.text: Mastercard bills acquirers, so payfacs and ISOs see scheme fees only as their acquirer passes them on.

tools_and_screens.name: Third-party billing monitors
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Platforms that track Mastercard billing lines, bulletins and penalties for issuers and acquirers.

friction.text: Acquirer misreadings of Mastercard fee triggers have over and underbilled merchants.

how_it_works.text: Payfacs under $250 million a year in Amex volume register through a certified OptBlue Participant and get single-source statement, servicing and settlement.
Reconciliation records carry a Seller ID so a payment aggregator can match fees and pricing to each sub-merchant.
Processor guides price OptBlue charges by MCC industry and ticket size, with three levels per industry and dearer levels for keyed or non-US cards.
The Amex network fee on OptBlue settled sales rose from 0.15% in First Data's 2018 guide to 0.165% in Fiserv's Fall 2025 guide.
Participants must give merchants statements whose pricing disclosures are clear and easy to understand.

friction.text: An OptBlue merchant bears the loss if its provider misprograms the POS and settlement goes to the wrong party.
Fiserv's Fall 2025 guide calls the Amex rates interchange, although the OptBlue regulations say the wholesale fee is not interchange.
Processor guides warn that terminals or software sending data wrongly can cost merchants the best pricing level.

how_it_works.text: Discover reaches payfac and ISO merchants through acquirer pricing, which a large acquirer sets as a blended rate for Discover.

friction.text: A merchant services firm says merchants on flat or tiered plans cannot see migrated Discover debit rates on their statements.

how_it_works.text: Under the sponsor model, network standards bar processors such as Global Payments from performing funds settlement or touching merchant settlement funds.
A payfac settles funds daily to each sub-merchant, and a sponsor bank says funding reconciliation is more burdensome in that model.
Stripe charges network costs to a platform and recovers them from each connected account within hours.

tools_and_screens.name: Stripe IC+ plan-level report for connected accounts

SMS settlement cuts off at 8 pm Pacific for Interlink and 10 pm Pacific for Visa and Plus. Every SMS report header shows the online settlement date.
Through the day the system keeps running totals of counts and amounts every 30 minutes. It stores them as 0520 advices for the processor to recover.

how_it_works.text: US Mastercard ATM interchange pays USD 0.35 for Tier 1 issuers, USD 0.45 for Tier 2 and USD 0.50 base per withdrawal.
Tiers are reset every quarter from the issuer's settled ATM volume.
In Europe a late presentment fee applies to ATM first presentments older than 45 days.
On Mastercard's debit switch, processors settle with terminal owners themselves. The switch settles only with each processor, per the 2006 manual.
Debit switch transactions received after day end settle on the next business day.
In 2006 the debit switch day ended at 07:00 New York time for Debit Mastercard and 15:00 for Maestro and Cirrus.

Operators reconcile per terminal, matching withdrawals, surcharge and settlement dates to deposits and allowing for funds in transit.
Revenue splits are fixed before a terminal goes live, through an installation worksheet, ACH authorisations and a voided cheque.
Networks set both the interchange issuers pay and the amount paid to a deployer.
A credit union ATM settlement analyst balances ATM general ledgers daily, and bank fleets balance from a terminal transaction detail report.

how_it_works.text: Amex settles directly signed US merchants by ACH, paying submissions less discount, fees and chargebacks on a one, three, fifteen or thirty day plan.

design_moves.title: Every fee line traces to its trigger
design_moves.move: Give each invoice line a stable billing identifier, a plain description, its trigger rule and a link to the transactions behind it. Make it downloadable as data at no charge.
design_moves.why_advantage: Visa and Mastercard told the UK regulator they cannot supply this within a year. Portal codes that differ from invoice codes are a documented acquirer complaint. Mastercard's SWCHD586-A already groups debit fees by message type and function code, with a net fees page for each processor.

design_moves.title: Show the class and rate each transaction was billed at
partner_types: Merchants where they touch the network directly
design_moves.move: Per transaction, show the card class, the interchange programme priced and cleared, and the reason for any downgrade, kept for the retention period.
design_moves.why_advantage: The Fed found Discover charged a commercial rate for sixteen years without telling merchants. Cybersource already shows priced against cleared with a reason code. OptBlue puts most fees in the GRRCN file, while the rate table stays in an appendix Participants may not publish. Visa's SMS detail reports can print each transaction's fee level and jurisdiction, yet that line is off by default and changed only through a representative.

design_moves.title: Totals that tie to the wire
design_moves.move: State the settlement arithmetic on screen and guarantee that report totals equal the funds moved, with the tie-out shown for each day.
design_moves.why_advantage: Issuers rebuild Mastercard fund reconciliation from fragments. Amex, Mastercard Send and Discover's own old report show the tie-out can be promised. Mastercard's Transfer Agent Advisement Detail shows one section per member ID within one payment, a working model for tying ledgers to a single wire. Mastercard's 2006 switch manual says SWCHD363 amounts should match the settlement records, and urges processors to automate the daily compare.

design_moves.title: Settlement day as a status
design_moves.move: Show each settlement day as pending or complete, with each file's delivery state and a proactive notice when a network file is late. Show committed service levels only.
design_moves.why_advantage: Late network files are the main cause of processor delays, and Mastercard makes senders phone to confirm a file. Stripe and Lithic already treat completeness as a state. Mastercard already emails opt-in open settlement notices, yet a missed notice does not stop daily assessments from USD 250. Visa's single message system already keeps 30-minute running totals as 0520 advices, a working base for an intraday settlement status.

design_moves.title: Change notice names the billing line
design_moves.move: Announce each fee change six months ahead with the billing identifier it will appear under, and offer an impact estimate on the partner's own past volume.
design_moves.why_advantage: Visa bulletins omitted billing events, so fees appeared first on invoices. UK rules now require six months' notice and on-request impact models. OptBlue already commits to 180 days' written notice before wholesale fees change, a lead time a network could publish per fee line.

design_moves.title: Fix billing errors for everyone
partner_types: Merchants where they touch the network directly
design_moves.move: When the network finds a billing error, correct it for every affected partner, show the correction beside the original line and say when it will settle.
design_moves.why_advantage: The RBA expects this. Mastercard sought to claw back years of fees after its own error, and Discover's refunds are still being allocated years later.

design_moves.title: Keep the short bill
design_moves.move: Carry the one-page invoice and single-point gateway settlement into the portal as the default view, with one line per network and detail on demand.
design_moves.why_advantage: Community banks and credit unions complain of long, error-prone bills and thin teams.

design_moves.title: Publish the money rulebook
design_moves.move: Publish one public page of settlement timing, exception handling, fee amounts and standard acquirer and ATM rates, with dated future changes. Publishing US rates is a business decision.
design_moves.why_advantage: Amex GNS and Interac already publish this. Discover keeps US acquirer rates behind a code, and PULSE gives no ATM amounts. Visa's VSS guide and Mastercard's Settlement Manual are marked confidential or proprietary, yet 2018 and 2020 copies are openly readable on a document-sharing site.

design_moves.title: An ATM statement by terminal and network
design_moves.move: Give operators and their processors a per-terminal view of interchange by network, net of network fees, with each fee named and its rate shown.
design_moves.why_advantage: Operators say networks set interchange and fees pass through unevenly. Many reconcile in spreadsheets, and the study found no network offering operators this view directly.

design_moves.title: The same data as file and API
design_moves.move: Offer settlement, invoice and interchange data both as files and as an API with completeness flags, so processors stop rebuilding it for each client.
design_moves.why_advantage: Mastercard's public catalogue has no settlement or billing API, and Adyen's delayed-fee report has none. Programme managers each build their own wrapper. Mastercard sends the same advisement by Connect, email, fax or SWIFT MT998, and Visa offers every VSS report as TC 46 data or TC 47 print. Visa lets SMS members take the same activity as formatted reports or as 130-byte raw data records.
